title: Contest a speeding or parking ticket with a written defense
summary: Give your bot a photo of the ticket and your side of the story. It works out how to contest it, writes the defense, and tracks the deadline.
what_the_bot_does: Reads the ticket and pulls out the violation, date, place, fine and the deadline to respond.
Finds the official way to contest it for that city or state (online, by mail or in person).
Asks you what actually happened and what proof you have, such as photos, receipts or signs.
Writes a short, factual written defense and a checklist of what to attach.
Shows you everything before anything is filed, then reminds you before the deadline.
what_you_end_up_with: A ready-to-submit written defense, the right place to file it, and a reminder before the deadline.

tools.note: The shared example used Grok Bot

prompt: Here's a photo of my [speeding/parking] ticket from [city, state]. What happened: [your honest account]. Proof I have: [photos, receipts, witnesses]. 1) Tell me the deadline to respond and the official way to contest it, with a link to the official page. 2) Write a short, factual written defense using only what I've told you. Don't invent facts. 3) List what I should attach. Don't submit anything or pay anything without asking me first.
watch_out: One person's win isn't a guarantee. The shared example is a single DC ticket, and rules and odds differ by city and state.
Only state facts that are true. You sign what gets submitted, not the bot.
Check the deadline on the ticket itself. Missing it can add late fees.
Blur or remove your personal details before sharing screenshots. The poster had the bot anonymize his.

title: Dispute an error on your credit report
summary: Your credit report shows an account, late payment or balance that isn't right. AI can help you spot the mistakes and write a clear dispute letter in minutes.
problem: Your credit report shows an account, late payment or balance that isn't right, and you don't know how to get it fixed.
outcome: A list of the likely errors on your report, the proof you need for each, and ready-to-send dispute letters for the credit bureau and the business that reported it.
what_the_bot_does: Get your free reports from Equifax, Experian and TransUnion at AnnualCreditReport.com (free every week, and checking doesn't hurt your score).
Remove your Social Security number, birth date and full account numbers, then paste the report sections into the prompt.
Let the AI list every item that looks wrong and say what proof would back up each one.
Have it draft one letter to each credit bureau that shows the mistake, and one to the business that reported it, following the FTC's checklist.
Send by certified mail with a return receipt (or use the bureau's online dispute form), keep copies, and put a reminder on your calendar for 30 days later.
what_you_end_up_with: A list of the likely errors on your report, the proof you need for each, and ready-to-send dispute letters for the credit bureau and the business that reported it.
time_saved: Editor's estimate: about an hour of reading and letter writing
prompt:
Help me dispute errors on my credit report. I have removed my Social Security number, birth date and full account numbers.

Credit bureau: [EQUIFAX / EXPERIAN / TRANSUNION]
Report sections I think are wrong: [PASTE]
What I believe is true, and the proof I have: [e.g. 'paid in full on 3/2025, have the bank statement' / 'never opened this account']

1. List each item that looks inaccurate or incomplete, and say why in one line.
2. For each, tell me what document would best prove it.
3. Draft a short dispute letter to the credit bureau that names each item, says why it's wrong, asks for it to be corrected or deleted, and lists the copies I'm enclosing. Leave [brackets] for my name and address.
4. Draft a matching letter to the business that reported it.
Don't invent facts or laws. If something might be identity theft, tell me to go to IdentityTheft.gov.
watch_out: Correct but negative information (like a real late payment) can't be disputed away. The FTC says most of it can stay on your report for seven years, and bankruptcies for 10.
Never paste your Social Security number or full account numbers into a chatbot. Add them to the printed letter yourself.
Disputing is free. Be wary of credit repair companies that charge up front to do what you can do yourself.
AI can misread a report. Check every item it flags against the report itself before you send anything.

faq.q: How long does a credit bureau have to investigate my dispute?
faq.a: The FTC says the credit bureau has 30 days to investigate, however you filed the dispute. It must send you the results in writing, plus a free copy of your report if anything changed.

faq.q: Does it cost anything to dispute a credit report error?
faq.a: No. Both the credit bureau and the business that reported the information have to correct wrong or incomplete information for free.

faq.q: Should I dispute with the credit bureau or the business?
faq.a: The FTC recommends both: dispute with each credit bureau that shows the mistake, and with the business that supplied the information.

faq.q: Can I use ChatGPT to dispute my credit report?
faq.a: Yes, for the reading and the writing: spotting likely errors and drafting the letters. You still send the dispute yourself, by mail or the bureau's own website, and you should leave sensitive numbers out of the chat.

title: Question a medical bill that looks wrong
problem: A doctor or hospital bill is higher than you expected and you can't tell what you're paying for.
outcome: A plain-English breakdown of every line, a list of charges worth questioning, and a polite request for a corrected bill.
prompt:
Help me understand and question a medical bill. Personal details are removed.

Itemized bill (codes, descriptions, amounts): [PASTE]
What my insurance paid / my EOB says: [PASTE OR 'NO INSURANCE']

1. Explain each line in plain English.
2. Flag anything that looks like a duplicate, a service I may not have received, or a charge that doesn't match my EOB.
3. List questions to ask the billing office.
4. Draft a short, polite letter asking for a review and a corrected bill, and asking them to hold the bill from collections while it's reviewed.
Mark anything you're unsure about.
time_saved: Editor's estimate: about 30 minutes to go through a long bill line by line
steps: Call the billing office and ask for a fully itemized bill with billing codes.
Remove personal details and paste the bill and your EOB into the prompt.
Check each flagged line against your own records and your insurer's EOB.
Send the letter, and write down who you talked to and when.
If you were uninsured or got a surprise out-of-network bill, read the federal No Surprises rules at CMS.
watch_out: AI can be wrong about billing rules. Treat its flags as questions to ask, not facts.

Remove Social Security numbers, account numbers, member IDs and birth dates before you paste or upload anything. In ChatGPT you can use Temporary Chat or turn off “Improve the model for everyone” under Settings › Data controls.

faq.a: A bill that lists each service, supply and medicine separately, usually with billing codes. Summary bills often hide mistakes, so ask for the itemized version.

title: Find and cancel subscriptions you forgot about
problem: You're paying for apps and memberships you don't use, and cancelling each one is a maze.
outcome: A list of every recurring charge, which ones to cancel, and either the cancellation done by an agent or exact steps for each.
prompt:
Here are my last 2–3 months of card/bank transactions (account numbers removed):
[PASTE TRANSACTIONS]

1. List every recurring charge: name, amount, how often, and yearly cost.
2. Mark which look like subscriptions I might not use.
3. For each one I choose to cancel: [LIST], give me the exact cancellation steps (website path or phone), or if you can use websites, go to the official site and cancel it, asking me before the final click.
4. Remind me to check for a confirmation email for each.

tools.note: Can go through a cancellation flow on the website and ask before the final step.

time_saved: Editor's estimate: 15–30 minutes to audit a few months of statements
steps: Download or copy 2–3 months of transactions. Remove account numbers.
Paste them into the prompt and review the recurring list.
Decide what to cancel. Watch for annual plans that just renewed.
Cancel through the official site or app store, or let an agent do it with your approval.
Save each confirmation email until the next statement shows no charge.
watch_out: Cancel only through the company's real site or your app store, never through a link in an unexpected email.
Never paste card numbers or passwords into a chat.

faq.q: What about subscriptions billed through my phone?
faq.a: Those are managed in your Apple or Google account settings, not on the company's website. Ask the AI for the exact menu path for your phone.
